sources.license: US Government work; NIST states that information on its sites is public information and may be distributed or copied, with credit requested

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only for the facts that confidence limits for the mean are an interval estimate formed as the estimate plus and minus a multiplier times the standard error; that a 95% confidence interval does not mean a 95% probability that the interval contains the true mean, because the level of confidence is associated with the method of calculating the interval and the confidence coefficient is the proportion of samples of a given size expected to contain the true mean; and that the interval narrows as the sample size grows through the square-root term and widens as the sample standard deviation grows. All wording, the cohort, and every worked example here are original. NIST copyright guidance at https://www.nist.gov/oism/copyrights states that NIST information is public information that may be distributed or copied and requests appropriate credit.

sources.license: US Government work; NIST states that information on its sites is public information and may be distributed or copied, with credit requested

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only for the facts that a confidence interval provides a range of values likely to contain the population parameter of interest; that if the same population is sampled on numerous occasions and interval estimates made each time, the resulting intervals would bracket the true population parameter in approximately 95% of cases at that level; and that a two-sided interval brackets the parameter from above and below while a one-sided interval supplies a single bound. All expression, examples and arithmetic in this lesson are original. NIST copyright guidance at https://www.nist.gov/oism/copyrights states that NIST information is public information that may be distributed or copied and requests appropriate credit.

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only for the facts that comparing the means of two independent samples with equivalent standard deviations uses a pooled standard deviation with the factor sqrt(1/N1 + 1/N2), that the assumption of equivalent standard deviations should be tested before it is made, and that the associated degrees of freedom are N1 + N2 - 2. sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Food and Drug Administration
sources.version: PDF retrieved from the FDA guidance library on 2026-07-25; cover states September 1998. The later ICH E9(R1) addendum on estimands does not alter the passages relied on here.
sources.locator: Section V.E, Estimation, Confidence Intervals, and Hypothesis Testing (5.5); section III.C.2 on equivalence and noninferiority margins; section VI.D on safety and tolerability; and the Glossary entry for frequentist methods
sources.license: US Government work as published by the FDA; the underlying guidance was developed by the International Conference on Harmonisation

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only for the facts that estimates of treatment effects should be accompanied by confidence intervals whenever possible with the method of calculation identified in advance; that two-sided confidence intervals are generally appropriate for estimating the possible size of the difference between two treatments; that for equivalence trials two-sided intervals should be used and equivalence is inferred when the entire confidence interval falls within equivalence margins whose choice must be justified clinically; that for safety and tolerability the use of confidence intervals is preferred to hypothesis testing because the imprecision arising from low frequencies of occurrence is then clearly demonstrated; and that the guidance glossary defines frequentist methods, naming confidence intervals among them, as methods interpreted in terms of the frequency of certain outcomes occurring in hypothetical repeated realizations of the same experimental situation. No sentence, table or example from the guidance is reproduced or closely paraphrased in learner-facing prose; the dinner-timing service, the invented threshold, and the blood-pressure trial are original.
